newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac promises Romania strong support on NATO bid.
newsitem.headline: Chirac promises Romania strong support on NATO bid.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac told Romanian President President Emil Constantinescu on Wednesday that Paris strongly backed Bucharest's drive to be among the first East European nations to join NATO.

"I confirmed to President Constantinescu that France would plead strongly with its allies for Romania to be among the first four or five countries to join NATO," Chirac said after an hour-long meeting with Constantinescu in Paris.
He did not name any of the other candidates from the former East bloc.

Chirac said he "favoured the entry (of Romania) in the first wave of NATO's expansion, which should in principle be discussed or decided in Madrid on July 7". He told reporters Bucharest's drive was "legitimate" and "justified".
Romania's bid for early membership of NATO, once a long shot behind favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, has gained ground in recent weeks largely because of French support.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said last month that Paris would back Bucharest.
Constantinescu, touring European capitals on his first trip to the West since he beat ex-communists in elections in November, said he had found a "great friend of Romania" in Chirac.
Chirac is to visit Romania on February 20 and 21, the first Western leader to travel to Romania since the elections.
"Our hopes are tied to his actions, especially concerning integration into NATO," Constantinescu said. "I thank President Chirac for what he has done and we are joyfully awaiting his visit."

Chirac saId France would help Romania's efforts to join the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) "which is the immediate problem, but also the European Union, which we strongly desire".
